title: Chapter 9 summary and quiz
recap: A reliable workflow separates input recovery from domain calculations. The reader decides whether a value is syntactically valid and in range; the pricing function applies the business rules without touching a stream.
Test each unit and then the whole sequence. Include invalid-first attempts, endpoint values, and EOF at every stage so the program cannot silently loop forever or reuse stale data.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Build a resilient order workflow. readBounded(low,high) follows 9.5 line-reading rules but accepts the inclusive bounds; return -1 on EOF or low > high. orderTotal(code,quantity) accepts product codes 1/2/3 priced at 5/8/12 and quantities 1..20; invalid values return -1. placeOrder() reads a product in [1,3], then quantity in [1,20], and returns the total, or -1 if input ends. Do not print prompts or totals; return the result. Retrying a quantity must not reread the product.
hints: Reuse the extraction/recovery pattern in a bounds-parameterized reader.
Validate both pricing arguments before calculating.
In placeOrder, stop immediately if either read returns the EOF sentinel.
